reason: The multi-disciplinary assessment correctly identifies immediate life-threatening risks: Grade 4 neutropenia predisposing to septic shock, Grade 3 thrombocytopenia with bleeding risk, and progressive anemia causing hemodynamic instability. Advanced age and ECOG 2 further reduce physiologic reserve. Urgent interventions (G-CSF, platelet transfusion, infection surveillance) are critical for patient safety.
evidences: Grade 4 neutropenia requires immediate G-CSF and broad-spectrum antibiotics
Platelet count <50,000/μL with bleeding risk mandates transfusion
Hemodynamic instability from anemia warrants urgent transfusion
